en.html:
I introduced myself as Shirou Kuniuji's messenger and asked for a meeting with Sakurako Okabe. The people of the Kyougoku household were taken aback. I also passed on Kuniuji's wish not to make a big thing of it, and in the end they let me through. Still, this would not pass with nothing happening afterward.

Even so, it was better than Kuniuji Ashikaga himself appearing without warning, and I could hardly sneak in. So it was a matter of necessity. Discreet questions would probably be pointed at Kuniuji now.

He would know this. Knowing it, he must have wished for it all the same.

en.html:
I sat down at a suitable spot and told her in short how I had come to know Kuniuji. A strange story, certainly. But she herself had seen that high-born boy at his football, so making her understand was not difficult.

While talking, I let my eyes go round the room and took its measure. No iron bars. No window that was only a tiny slit for light. It was an ordinary room.

Even if it was not her own chamber, the ease with which she sat in it said it belonged to her living quarters. Then the conditions of her custody did not seem so harsh. Walks, as before, were apparently allowed.

...But I did not mistake this softness for kindness. Not one grain of it, I judged, came from concern for her health of body or mind.

Rokuhara fears that Princess Sakurako will meet the anti-shogunate camp. That is exactly why it placed her here in Fudaraku. And yet, on the other side, it must also be hoping for exactly that. If both sides make contact and move, the whole lot can be caught in one net.

A lighter guard around her need not cause trouble. After all, escape from this castle was impossible. No need for excessive vigilance: they could dispense with it and use her as bait for bigger fish. Rokuhara was cunning in every small thing.

ja.html:
適当に座って、俺は邦氏との奇縁を手短に説明した。
　妙といえば随分と妙な話であった筈だが、あの高貴
な少年が蹴球を嗜む様は彼女も目撃していたので理解
させるに難は無かった。

　話しつつ、視線を流して部屋の様子を観察する。
　別に鉄格子で囲われている事はないし、窓が明かり
取りの小窓だけなどという事もない。

　普通の部屋だった。
　ここが彼女の居室ではないにしても、部屋に慣れた
様子からして居住空間の一部であるのは確かと思える。
となると、姫の環境はそう厳しいものでも無さそうだ。

　先日の通り、散歩なども許されているらしい。
　
　……だがこの緩やかな待遇は、決して彼女の心身の
健康を思いやっての事ではないだろう。

　六波羅は桜子姫と反幕勢力との接触を警戒している。
なればこそこの普陀楽に置いたのだ。
　しかし一方で期待もしている筈だ――両者が接触し
行動を起こせば、一網打尽だと。

　桜子の身辺を手薄にしてもさして問題はない。<ruby>結局<rt>・・</rt></ruby>
<ruby>のところ<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>、この城内から脱出するなど不可能だからだ。
　必要もない厳戒態勢を捨て、大魚を誘い出す釣り餌
としている。全く、六波羅はいちいち狡猾であった。

en.html:
Taken literally, it was an outrageous thing to say. The Ashikaga heir and the surviving daughter of Okabe: positions so far apart that comparing them was plain foolishness.

Still, Princess Sakurako did not dismiss it in a single word. She lowered her eyes to the stock and sank into thought.

Was she recalling that brief meeting of the other day, hardly more than a passing by?

In the princess's eyes I seemed to see the boy's flushed cheeks.

In the princess's eyes I seemed to see the boy's flushed cheeks.

en.html:
I avoided spending more words. I did not wish to say anything beyond fact. I had not come to talk the princess round.

About that boy's figure and its shadow, I had many more thoughts. But blown from my mouth into her ear, they would mean nothing.

Only what she learned by herself would become truth. And that road did not seem a long one.

I limited my answer to a bow of the head.

It could not be simple. Even if the two of them wished it, would those around them allow it? No. Not at all likely.

It might become a road harder than walking alone. But if, despite that, they chose to walk close together—

They would not be lonely. Compared with going alone, the road would feel a little less cold.
